notes.title: Welcome to Devot
notes.bodyMd:
This is your library. Everything you write stays on this device, in a database in the app's data folder, and nothing is sent anywhere. Delete this notebook whenever you like: it will not come back.

## Organize

- **Notebooks** hold notes and can nest. Make one with the _New Notebook_ button in the sidebar, and drag notebooks and notes to move them.
- **Tags** go on any note from the command palette (⌘K). Click a tag in the sidebar to filter the list by it.
- **Status** marks where a note stands: None ⌃⌘1, Active ⌃⌘2, On Hold ⌃⌘3, Completed ⌃⌘4, Dropped ⌃⌘5.
- **Pin to Top** keeps a note at the top of its list (P in the note list).
- **Templates** start a note from a note of your own: New Note from Template, ⌘T.
- Deleted notes wait in the **Trash** (⌘⌫ in the note list) until you empty it.

## Write

Each note has four views: _Show Write Mode_, _Show Editor_, _Show Editor and Preview_ and _Show Preview_. Write Mode renders the note as you write, revealing the Markdown of the element under the caret. The editor shows all your Markdown with its syntax highlighted; the preview shows the result and scrolls along with the editor.

| Do this                       | Press                                                                           |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| New note                      | ⌘N                                                                |
| Bold, italic, strikethrough   | ⌘B, ⌘I, ⌘U        |
| Inline code, code block       | ⌥⌘E, ⇧⌘C                                   |
| Link                          | ⌥⌘K                                                             |
| Headings 1 to 6               | ⌘1 to ⌥⌘6                              |
| Bulleted, numbered, task list | ⇧⌘L, ⇧⌘O, ⇧⌘T |
| Quote                         | ⌘'                                                            |

Type `/` at the start of a line for a menu of everything you can insert, and `[[` to link to another note by its title. Paste or drop an image to attach it to the note. See **The Long Way Home** note in this notebook for every kind of Markdown Devot understands.

## Find your way

- **Command palette** ⌘K: every command, notes, notebooks and tags in one list.
- **Find in the note** ⌘F, and replace ⌥⌘F.
- **Search** the library ⇧⌘F, or all notes ⌥⇧⌘F. Searching understands words, phrases and filters such as notebook and tag names.
- **Back and forward** between notes: ⌘[ and ⌘]. Next and previous note: ⇧⌘] and ⇧⌘[.
- **Hide the sidebar** ⌘/, **Focus Mode** ⇧⌘D, and the text size ⌘= bigger, ⌘- smaller, ⌘0 back to normal.
- **History** ⌥⌘Y lists the versions of a note and shows what changed between them.

## Your data

- Devot backs up the library every day and keeps the last seven backups (_Backups_ in the command palette).
- The **Markdown Mirror** keeps a folder of plain `.md` files in step with your notes, if you choose one in the command palette.
- Any note exports as Markdown, HTML or PDF from its menu, and a Markdown folder can be imported.
- Notebooks are closed to AI tools until you switch _Allow AI Access_ on for a notebook.

Have a look at [The Long Way Home](devot://note/00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000012) next.

notes.title: 🕊️ The Long Way Home
notes.bodyMd:
---
title: Markdown example
description: A tour of the Markdown Devot understands, told by a homing pigeon
tags: [example, markdown]
---

*A homing pigeon's field notes, and a tour of everything Devot can render.*

Everything below is plain Markdown. Open this note in the editor (*Show Editor* or *Show Editor and Preview*) to see how each piece is written. The block above, between the two `---` lines, is *front matter*: Devot shows it in a box at the top of the preview.

## Contents

- [Headings](#headings)
- [Text](#text)
- [Lists and tasks](#lists-and-tasks)
- [Quotes and alerts](#quotes-and-alerts)
- [Links and images](#links-and-images)
- [Tables](#tables)
- [Code](#code)
- [Math](#math)
- [Diagrams](#diagrams)
- [Plugins](#plugins)
- [Footnotes](#footnotes)
- [Rules, symbols and escapes](#rules-symbols-and-escapes)

---

## Headings

Six levels, from the whole journey down to a single feather:

# Day 1: Released at the Coast

## The basket opened at dawn

### She circled the field twice

#### found the sun over her left wing

##### and the wind off the sea

###### then turned for home

---

## Text

**Pidge** was a homing pigeon, and a *very* punctual one. She carried notes, not letters: ~~long letters~~ short notes, written in Markdown, rolled up in a ring on her leg. Some words mattered more than others, so the writer marked them **bold**, *italic*, ***both at once***, or <mark>highlighted</mark> so they would not be missed.

The note on her leg read `meet at the old tower, 6pm`. To send another, the writer pressed <kbd>⌘N</kbd>; to find an old one, <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd>.

She flew at 10<sup>3</sup> metres, through air thick with H<sub>2</sub>O, and arrived to applause: :tada: :sparkles: :bird:

A line that ends with two spaces  
continues on the next line,  
the way a pigeon keeps going after a short rest.

A blank line starts a new paragraph.

---

## Lists and tasks

### What Pidge packs for a flight

- **Navigation**
  - The sun, by day
  - The Earth's magnetic field, always
    - felt rather than seen
    - steady even under cloud
  - Landmarks: rivers, roads, the old tower
- **Supplies**
  - One rolled-up note
  - Nothing else; weight matters

### The route, in order

1. **Leave the coast**
   1. Circle to get bearings
   2. Pick the heading
2. **Cross the valley**
   - Ride the warm air over the fields
   - Skip the hawk's ridge
3. **Rest on the bridge**
4. **Arrive at the loft**

### Pidge's flight log

Task lists show check boxes:

- [x] Read the welcome note
- [x] Open the Markdown example
- [x] Leave the coast
- [ ] Reach the loft before dark
  - [x] Cross the valley
  - [x] Rest on the bridge
  - [ ] Find the window left open
- [ ] Write a first note of your own

---

## Quotes and alerts

The keeper wrote this on the loft wall:

> A pigeon does not know the map.
> She knows the way home,
> and that is *better*.

Quotes nest when you add more `>`:

> Where are you going?
>> Home.
>>> How do you know where that is?

GitHub-style alerts get a colour and an icon:

> [!NOTE]
> Homing pigeons can find their way back from hundreds of kilometres away.

> [!TIP]
> Type `[[` in the editor to link to any note by its title.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Pictures you paste or drop are stored with the note, so the note travels with everything it needs.

> [!WARNING]
> Hawk on the ridge. Fly around it.

> [!CAUTION]
> Don't open the loft window during a storm.

---

## Links and images

A [web link](https://example.com) opens in your browser, and a link to a note stays inside Devot: back to [Welcome to Devot](devot://note/00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000011). A bare address such as https://example.com becomes a link as well. Headings are link targets too, so you can jump back to [Text](#text).

![A sample picture](devot://file/00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000013#half)

After the address, `#small`, `#half` or `#full` sets an image's size (also in the image's context menu):

![Small](devot://file/00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000013#small)

---

## Tables

### The loft roster

| Pigeon     | Role       | Favourite saying                 |
| ---------- | ---------- | -------------------------------- |
| **Pidge**  | Courier    | "Home is a direction."           |
| **Rook**   | Navigator  | "Follow the river."              |
| **Biscuit**| Lookout    | "Hawk! Hawk! Oh, it's a leaf."   |
| **Old Gus**| Keeper     | "Every note arrives eventually." |

### Delivery record

Colons in the divider row set alignment: left, centre, right.

| Route              | Distance | Days | Delivered |
| :----------------- | -------: | :--: | :-------: |
| Coast → Loft       |   120 km |  1   |    ✅     |
| Mountains → Loft   |   310 km |  2   |    ✅     |
| City → Loft        |    45 km |  1   |    ❌     |
| Island → Loft      |   480 km |  3   |    ✅     |

While the cursor is in a table, Tab moves to the next cell, and Format Table in the command palette lines the columns up.

---

## Code

A fenced block takes a language, and a `title` for its heading bar:

```ts title="flight.ts"
interface Note {
  title: string
  tags: string[]
}

type Heading = 'north' | 'south' | 'east' | 'west'

export function deliver(note: Note, heading: Heading): string {
  return `Carrying "${note.title}" ${heading} (${note.tags.length} tags)`
}
```

```python title="homing.py"
import math

def bearing_home(lat: float, lon: float, home: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
    """Compass bearing from where Pidge is to the loft, in degrees."""
    d_lon = math.radians(home[1] - lon)
    lat1, lat2 = math.radians(lat), math.radians(home[0])
    x = math.sin(d_lon) * math.cos(lat2)
    y = math.cos(lat1) * math.sin(lat2) - math.sin(lat1) * math.cos(lat2) * math.cos(d_lon)
    return (math.degrees(math.atan2(x, y)) + 360) % 360
```

```rust title="loft.rs"
fn main() {
    let roster = ["Pidge", "Rook", "Biscuit"];
    for name in roster {
        println!("{name} is home");
    }
}
```

```json title="note.json"
{
  "title": "Meet at the old tower",
  "time": "18:00",
  "urgent": true
}
```

```sh
pnpm install
```

A block without a language is plain text:

```
no highlighting, no title
just the words, the way they were written
```

Inline code fits in a sentence: Pidge's ring is tagged `ring.id = 0042`.

---

## Math

Inline math sits in a sentence, like $E = mc^2$, or Pidge's average speed $\bar{v} = \frac{d}{t}$. A display block has its own line:

$$
\bar{v} = \frac{120\ \text{km}}{2.5\ \text{h}} = 48\ \text{km/h}
$$

The great-circle distance home, by the haversine formula:

$$
d = 2r \arcsin\left(\sqrt{\sin^2\frac{\Delta\varphi}{2} + \cos\varphi_1 \cos\varphi_2 \sin^2\frac{\Delta\lambda}{2}}\right)
$$

And the odds that a note eventually arrives:

$$
P(\text{arrive}) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left(1 - (1 - p)^n\right) = 1 \quad \text{for any } p > 0
$$

---

## Diagrams

### The flight, as a flowchart

A `mermaid` block draws a diagram:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Released at the coast] --> B{Sun visible?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Steer by the sun]
  B -->|No| D[Steer by the magnetic field]
  C --> E[Cross the valley]
  D --> E
  E --> F{Hawk on the ridge?}
  F -->|Yes| G[Fly around it]
  F -->|No| H[Straight over]
  G --> I[Rest on the bridge]
  H --> I
  I --> J[Home at the loft]
```

### A note's life, as a sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant W as Writer
  participant D as Devot
  participant P as Pidge
  W->>D: Write a note
  D-->>W: Saved
  W->>P: Tie it to her ring
  P->>P: Fly home
  P-->>W: Delivered
```

### The loft, as UML

A `plantuml` block (or `puml`) draws UML locally:

```plantuml
@startuml
class Pigeon {
  -name: String
  -ring: Integer
  +fly(heading)
  +rest()
  +deliver(note)
}

class Note {
  -title: String
  -tags: String[]
  +render()
}

class Loft {
  -roster: Pigeon[]
  +welcome(pigeon)
}

Pigeon --> Note : carries
Loft o-- Pigeon : houses
@enduml
```

### Everything in this note, as a mind map

A `markmap` block turns a Markdown outline into a mind map:

```markmap
# Devot Markdown
## Writing
- Headings
- Bold, italic, highlight
- Lists and tasks
- Quotes and alerts
## Linking
- Web links
- Note links
- Images with sizes
## Structure
- Tables
- Code with titles
- Footnotes
## Rendering
- Math
- Mermaid
- PlantUML
- Markmap
## Plugins
- Graphviz
- Charts
- CSV and BibTeX
- Note Query
- Excalidraw
- Themes
```

All three render offline and are included in HTML and PDF exports. Markmap shows a static, fully expanded map with plain-text labels. PlantUML uses its built-in Smetana layout; external includes and libraries are not loaded.

---

## Plugins

Everything above is built in. Devot's official plugins draw a few more kinds of block, and none of them is installed until you ask for it: on the Mac, open _Settings > Plugins_, find the plugin under _Official Plugins_ and click its _Install_ button. Devot shows what the plugin asks for before anything is installed.

> [!NOTE]
> Without its plugin, a block below stays plain code. That is not an error: the note keeps the block as written, and it draws as soon as the plugin is on. A drawing travels with the note, so the iPhone shows what the Mac drew. Exports and printing show plugin blocks as code.

### The route, as a graph

The **Graphviz** plugin draws a `dot` block:

```dot
digraph route {
  rankdir=LR
  node [shape=box, style=rounded]
  Coast -> Valley -> Bridge -> Loft
  Valley -> Ridge [style=dashed, label="hawk?"]
  Ridge -> Bridge [style=dashed]
}
```

### A week of deliveries, as a chart

The **Charts** plugin draws a `chart` block, from rows of a label and numbers. `type: line` or `type: bar` and a `title:` go first:

```chart
type: line
title: Notes delivered
day, Pidge, Rook
Mon, 4, 2
Tue, 6, 3
Wed, 5, 5
Thu, 8, 4
Fri, 7, 6
```

### The roster, from CSV

The **CSV Tables** plugin shows a `csv` block as a table, and imports `.csv` and `.tsv` files as notes (_File > Import_):

```csv
Pigeon,Ring,Flights,Best time
Pidge,0042,128,2h 30m
Rook,0017,96,2h 55m
Biscuit,0108,12,4h 10m
```

### The keeper's reading list, from BibTeX

The **BibTeX References** plugin shows a `bibtex` block as a reference list, and imports `.bib` files:

```bibtex
@article{keeton1971,
  author  = {Keeton, William T.},
  title   = {Magnets Interfere with Pigeon Homing},
  journal = {Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences},
  year    = {1971},
  volume  = {68},
  number  = {1},
  pages   = {102--106}
}

@article{walcott1996,
  author  = {Walcott, Charles},
  title   = {Pigeon Homing: Observations, Experiments and Confusions},
  journal = {Journal of Experimental Biology},
  year    = {1996},
  volume  = {199},
  pages   = {21--27}
}
```

### Your notes, as a live table

The **Note Query** plugin turns a `query` block into a table or list of the notes that match, each linked to its note. It is drawn again whenever a note changes:

```query
TABLE notebook AS "Notebook", updated AS "Last changed"
SORT updated DESC
LIMIT 5
```

`FROM #tag` or `FROM "Notebook"` narrows it, and `WHERE` filters by `status`, dates or any front matter property, such as `WHERE tags contains "example"`.

### The loft, as a sketch

The **Excalidraw** plugin draws an `excalidraw` block as a hand-drawn sketch. The block holds the sketch as JSON, so it travels with the note, and an empty block is a blank page to start from. With the note open in the editor, _Edit_ on the drawing opens a whiteboard, and _Done_ writes the sketch back into the block:

```excalidraw
{
  "type": "excalidraw",
  "version": 2,
  "elements": [
    {"type": "rectangle", "x": 220, "y": 40, "width": 140, "height": 100, "roundness": {"type": 3}, "seed": 1},
    {"type": "text", "x": 266, "y": 75, "width": 48, "height": 30, "text": "Loft", "originalText": "Loft", "fontSize": 24, "seed": 2},
    {"type": "ellipse", "x": 0, "y": 60, "width": 90, "height": 60, "seed": 3},
    {"type": "text", "x": 18, "y": 78, "width": 54, "height": 25, "text": "Pidge", "originalText": "Pidge", "fontSize": 20, "seed": 4},
    {"type": "arrow", "x": 100, "y": 90, "width": 110, "height": 0, "points": [[0, 0], [110, 0]], "endArrowhead": "arrow", "seed": 5}
  ]
}
```

### Colours

Theme plugins (Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Dracula, Nord, Gruvbox, Solarized, Rosé Pine and One) add colour themes for light and dark. Once one is installed, choose its card in _Settings > Appearance_.

---

## Footnotes

Homing pigeons[^homing] have carried messages for thousands of years[^history]. They navigate with several senses at once[^senses], and a good one comes home almost every time.[^1] Footnotes collect at the end of the note, and they can be named anything.[^named]

[^homing]: Bred specifically to return to their home loft.

[^history]: Long before Markdown, and long before paper was cheap.

[^senses]: The sun, the Earth's magnetic field, landmarks, and possibly smell.

[^1]: Like this one, numbered.

[^named]: Written as `[^named]` in the text.

---

## Rules, symbols and escapes

Three ways to draw a horizontal rule:

---

***

___

Special characters come through as typed:

- En dash: Day 1–3
- Em dash: Pidge flew—without stopping—to the bridge
- Arrows: Coast → Loft ← City
- Ellipsis: almost home…
- Copyright: © The Loft

A backslash shows a Markdown character as itself: \*not italic\*, \# not a heading, \[not a link\].

---

> [!TIP]
> That's the tour. Press <kbd>⌘N</kbd> and send your own note home. 🕊️
